questions.question: Why are only 'final goods and services' counted when calculating Gross Domestic Product?
options: Because intermediate goods have zero monetary value in wholesale markets
Because government tax inspectors refuse to inspect raw material receipts
Because the value of final goods already includes the value of all intermediate goods used in making the final product
Because intermediate goods are only produced by foreign multinational companies
questions.explanation: The value of final goods already includes the value of all the intermediate goods that are used in making the final good. For instance, the value of biscuits (final good) already includes the value of flour, sugar, and oil (intermediate goods). Counting intermediate goods separately would lead to double counting.

A situation where more people work on a farm than necessary, such that removing some workers does not reduce total crop production
Workers who are unemployed during off-monsoon winter months

questions.explanation: Underemployment or disguised unemployment occurs when people are apparently working but all of them are made to work less than their potential. Even if you move a few people out, production will not be affected because they are surplus labour.

questions.question: In the NCERT case study comparing Kanta (office worker) and Kamal (grocery store assistant), why is Kamal considered to be in the unorganised sector?
options: Kamal receives a monthly provident fund statement from the central government
Kamal gets free medical treatment at an executive corporate hospital
Kamal works from 7:30 AM to 8:00 PM without overtime pay, gets no paid leave, has no formal appointment letter, and can be told to leave at any time
Kamal works only two hours on weekends
questions.explanation: Kamal works in a small grocery store without formal appointment, works long hours without overtime pay, receives no paid holidays, and has no job security. Hence, he is in the unorganised sector.

questions.question: What is the primary driving motivation behind economic activities undertaken by the Public Sector (such as Indian Railways and Post Office)?
options: Social welfare and public benefit at affordable, subsidized rates
Maximizing quarterly corporate profits for private equity shareholders
Eliminating all competition to create private business monopolies
Transferring state revenues to offshore foreign bank accounts
questions.explanation: Activities in the private sector are guided by the motive to earn profits. The purpose of the public sector is not just to earn profits. Governments raise money through taxes and other ways to meet expenses on the services rendered by it for public welfare.

questions.subtopic: Why Government Must Invest in Heavy Infrastructure
questions.question: Why does the public sector often undertake large infrastructure projects such as roads, railways, harbours and dams?
options: The private sector is constitutionally prohibited from using heavy machinery
Such projects can require very large investment, and charging the many users enough to recover the cost may be difficult; public provision can help make the facilities broadly available
Engineers refuse to work for private enterprises
Infrastructure has no effect on economic development
questions.explanation: NCERT explains that some facilities require large spending and it may be difficult to collect sufficient payments from the many people who use them. Government investment can therefore help make important infrastructure available to the public. This does not mean private firms can never participate in infrastructure projects.
